lines.heard: This clip tells us a stranger my name, my building and my phone number.
All fictional. But creators post clips like this everyday.
A name on a parcel. A society board behind you. A number you say out loud.
Most reduction tools look for a fixed list. Spaces. License plates. Cleans. Documents.
On my held out clips, that list found 0 of 4 planted leads.
So Veil asks a different question. What in this video could identify you?
Muse Spark looks at keyframes and proposes candidates, each with a reason. The notification shows a full name, the gold plate shows a surname and a flat number.
None of these is a face or a license plate. The model has to understand the scene.
SAM 3.1 tracks each one through every frame and the output covers exactly those regions.
With Spark in the loop, three out of four were found. Then I re-ran the whole pipeline three times. Discovery passed every run.
Then code checks the work. Veil decodes its own output and confirms the covers are really there.
It re-reads the output with local OCR and runs a face detector on sampled frames.
Models make mistakes. Here Sam put the name mask on a block of code.
Local OCR read the mask, found code instead of the name Spark claimed and threw it out.
Spoken numbers too. Muse. Voice Transcribe. Here's a phone number read out in Hindi. And Veil mutes it.
Then it transcribes the output again. No digit run left.
But voice still gets digits wrong and the mute window met my limit in only one of three runs.
That's the point. Veil lever says a video is saved.
Every item is covered, unresolved or not checked. And it tells you why.
In this run, two items are unresolved, a plate rack with gaps and a face-like region. Nothing was left unchecked.
I held myself to that too. I wrote a test gate before running it. It failed. And false flag still failed two of three reruns. It's all in the repo.
Every model call is on a ledger. 751 calls about $2.40 per clip.
Try it live. Read the receipt and decide before you post.
Models propose and code decides. Veil built solo with Muse Spark. SAM 3.1. Muse Voice.
